sentences.text: The genus name combines a reference to the Tethys Ocean and the group Hadrosauroidea, while the species name means "insular" or "of the island," referring to the animal's habitat on islands in the European Archipelago.

The holotype specimen, nicknamed "Antonio," is a mostly complete but crushed skeleton cataloged as SC 57021, and an additional extensive skeleton nicknamed "Bruno" (SC 57247) was found at the same site.
This dinosaur had a beak, hands formed into fleshy pads, and three-toed feet.
The total estimated body length is 4.5 meters, though some argue this figure is an overestimate.
Preparing the fossil specimen required 2,800 hours of work to remove it from the rock matrix.
The genus Tethyshadros was named and described by Dalla Vecchia in 2009.
The subadult holotype "Antonio" weighed approximately 338 kg, while the adult "Bruno" weighed between 514 and 584 kg.
The parent group of Tethyshadros is Telmatosauridae, and the genus belongs to the family Telmatosauridae.
In 2021, researchers placed Tethyshadros as the sister taxon to Fylax within the Hadrosauromorpha clade.
In 2026, Magyar and colleagues recovered Tethyshadros as the sister taxon to Kryptohadros using updated phylogenetic matrices.
Magyar et al. named the clade containing Tethyshadros, Kryptohadros, and Telmatosaurus as Telmatosauridae.
Tethyshadros lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Campanian age.
This dinosaur is found in the Lipica Formation near Trieste, Italy, and was previously thought to belong to the Liburnia Formation.
It is debated whether the holotype represented an adult or a subadult, with later assessments based on bone histology suggesting it was a subadult.
